 Paytm, MobiKwik, Pine Labs shares tumble up to 7% on reports of further UPI MDR delay. What's next?
 SECTIONS Paytm, MobiKwik, Pine Labs shares tumble up to 7% on reports of further UPI MDR delay. What's next? By Debaroti Adhikary , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 11:02:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Shares of Paytm, MobiKwik and Pine Labs fell after reports suggested that the rollout of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions could face further delays, potentially extending beyond the 2027 assembly elections in five states. The government is reportedly wary of a backlash from merchants and trade associations ahead of the polls.

 ETMarkets.com Paytm, MobiKwik and Pine Labs fell on reports that MDR charges on select UPI transactions could be delayed.
 Shares of fintech platforms Paytm, Mobikwik and Pine Labs sharply tumbled up to 7% on Thursday as multiple reports surfaced, saying that the implementation of the merchant discount rate (MDR) on select Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions may be delayed further, with some raising worries over the rollout being postponed to as late as the 2027 assembly elections in five states.
 Shares of One 97 Communications, the operator of UPI giant Paytm , tumbled 7% to trade at Rs 1,765 apiece on NSE. One Mobikwik Systems shares also dropped 7% to Rs 211.53 apiece, while Pine Labs shares fell nearly 6% to Rs 160 apiece on Thursday morning.
The possible delay of the UPI MDR fee till beyond the 2027 polls comes as the government remains cautious of a potential backlash from merchants and trade associations, The Financial Express reported citing industry sources. This comes as Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur are set to go to polls in the first half of next year.
This comes after the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) last month delayed the implementation of the MDR fee beyond Diwali, which led to a sharp drop in the shares of the fintech firms as they missed the key festive season. Earlier, the new fee structure was scheduled to take effect from October 15 onwards.
Also read | UPI MDR rollout deferred until after Diwali 
 Live Events
 The NPCI in September had announced that a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. However, it received strong criticism from retail traders’ associations, leading to delays.
 Sources told The Economic Times that the Payments Council of India (PCI) has made multiple representations to the finance ministry and NPCI, seeking an early announcement of the final implementation date for merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions.
 Also read | Payment firms seek early MDR rollout for select UPI transactions while they stay 18 months without incentives 
 Why are Paytm, Pine Labs shares crashing? 
Paytm and Pine Labs were seen as the biggest beneficiaries in the MDR regime, positioned to capture the larger absolute opportunity. Paytm had said the introduction of the fee will generate additional revenue from the merchant business for many of the payment transactions that were free earlier. Brokerages hiked their target prices and earnings estimates for the fintech platform following the announcement. 
Paytm is positioned to capture the larger absolute opportunity, with analysts estimating FY28 UPI MDR revenue of as much as Rs 1,160 crore, before the delays were announced. Pine Labs, with a smaller UPI base, could see a sharper impact on earnings, with the new revenue stream potentially contributing about 20% to its EBIT and profit before tax estimates.
Jefferies estimated that Pine Labs could generate Rs 1.6 billion of incremental revenue from UPI MDR in FY28. That would represent about 20% of its EBIT and profit before tax estimates, while the report’s sensitivity analysis indicates an impact of about 14% on adjusted EBITDA. This is why the reports on MDR rollout delays spooked investors, leading to a sharp drop in these stocks.
